candidates.title: Fleet-Level Optimization for Heterogeneous Device Provisioning in ML Model Deployments
candidates.venue: International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems Workshops
candidates.abstract: With the increasing popularity of machine learning (ML) applications, networked computing systems like cloud data-centres are facing rapidly growing demand for ML inference tasks. Expanding systems to meet these demands, however, can be both costly and environmentally unsustainable. While several computer architecture optimizations have been proposed to alleviate monetary and environmental costs, e.g., by reusing older devices or those less customized to ML workloads, the resulting cost and performance tradeoffs at a platform level have yet to be modelled. We have also observed a structure to inference latency, i.e. a single prefill phase and a decode phase of an a priori unknown number of repeated computations. For LLMs, the computation time of an inference task (dominated by output token inference) is correlated with the length of its input [1]. As shorter-input requests tend to return fewer tokens, it is possible to isolate these tasks and allocate them on dedicated devices; indeed, a form of this segmenting currently occurs in deployment. As such, it is possible to use older or slower computation units to handle this segment of demand.
candidates.reason: Carnegie Mellon University著者原著（HotEthics 2026配布版）は、LLM推論の入力長と実行時間の相関を利用して異種・旧世代計算機へ要求を配分するサーバーフリート設計を定式化する。デバイス種別ごとの構成比・台数を決定変数とし、推論要求の入力長分布と遅延SLOの分位点から線形制約を構築、金銭・炭素・水などの重み付き費用を線形計画で最小化する。LLM推論インフラの配置最適化へ直接貢献するためaccept。ただし決定論的な入力長―実行時間対応と固定需要を仮定した予備的理論モデルであり、実機評価や運用時の需要変動は未検証。
